The '''Venture Company Camp''' is located within a valley in the central mountain range of Stonetalon Mountains. It was the starting area for [[Goblin (playable)|goblin]] players until the release of [[patch 1.17.1]], after which it was replaced with [[Blackstone Island]].

Originally ran by a ragged [[Venture Company]] crew led by Foreman [[Nert Blastentom]], the crew ran afoul of faulty equipment, night elf environmentalists and cursed ruins in their mission, and deserted to join the Horde, where they formed the [[Durotar Labor Union]]. The Venture Company have finally arrived to check on Blastentom and his crew's mission, to find no trace of their (now-ex) employees. They've now dug open a way to the valley to find a clue to their whereabouts and to finish the mission that was tasked to them all that time ago: Drain the land of all of its resources.

unnamed grandfather }} Lady '''Vereesa Windrunner''' is the former Speaker of the [[Silvermoon Remnant]] and a current member of the [[Regency Council]] of [[Alah'Thalas]]. An elven ranger during the aftermath of the [[Second War]], she is the younger sister of [[Sylvanas Windrunner]], who led the defense of [[Quel'Thalas]] and would later become the Dark Lady of the Forsaken, and [[Alleria Windrunner]], hero of the Second War. Previously the Speaker of the Silvermoon Remnant, Vereesa was a key individual in gaining the re-acceptance of the High Elves into the [[Alliance]]. However, following the expansion of Alah'Thalas and the resettlement of the [[Thalassian Highlands]], Vereesa was deposed by the surviving Quel'dorei nobility, though she was included in the current [[Regency Council]] alongside [[Lor'themar Theron]], [[Astalor Sunsworn]] and [[Grand Magister Rommath]]. ==Biography== ===Day of the Dragon=== To Vereesa's disgust, her first major assignment as a ranger did not involve hunting down the [[orc]]s that had been trapped on the planet [[Azeroth]] in the wake of the Dark Portal's destruction. Instead, she was asked to escort a human wizard named [[Rhonin]] to [[Hasic]], one of the eastern ports of [[Lordaeron]]. She accomplished her mission only to discover that there were no ships available to take Rhonin to his ultimate destination: [[Khaz Modan]]. Rhonin claimed that his mission was minor and only required him to observe the orc presence in Khaz Modan. Yet, he remained unusually determined to fulfill it. He even appealed to a group of [[Wildhammer dwarf|Wildhammer dwarves]], asking them to fly him to Khaz Modan on one of their [[gryphon]]s. At first, the dwarves refused, for they trusted humans little and wizards even less. Yet Vereesa had grown fond of Rhonin, and she suspected that his mission was more important than he wanted to admit. Appealing to the dwarves, she persuaded them to fly both her and Rhonin to Khaz Modan. Although Rhonin was separated from her along the flight, she tracked him all the way to [[Grim Batol]], which was a Horde stronghold under the leadership of [[Nekros Skullcrusher]]. Using a magical artifact known as the [[Demon Soul]], Nekros had managed to enslave [[Alexstrasza]] and, through her, most of the [[red dragonflight]]. Thus, [[Korialstrasz]] had sent Rhonin to Grim Batol with instructions to free Alexstrasza. Disguised as a mage named Krasus, Korialstrasz did not truly hope that Rhonin would be able to liberate the Dragonqueen. Rather, Korialstrasz hoped to trick the Horde into believing that a full-scale invasion was about to occur. While the Horde evacuated Grim Batol, Korialstrasz planned to strike and free his queen. His plan backfired when the massive [[black dragon]] [[Deathwing]] unexpectedly showed up and began stealing Alexstrasza's eggs. In fact, Deathwing had helped Rhonin reach Grim Batol precisely for that reason: the insane [[Dragon Aspect]] wanted to bolster his own failing flight by kidnapping Alexstrasza's children and raising them as his own. However, the other Dragon Aspects arrived to stop Deathwing. With the help of Vereesa and a group of dwarves, Rhonin took the Demon Soul from Nekros and managed to destroy it. Their powers fully restored, Alexstrasza and the other Aspects attacked Deathwing and forced him to flee. After the battle, Vereesa and Rhonin toured the various kingdoms in the Eastern Kingdoms and grew closer in the process.''[[Day of the Dragon]]'' ===War of the Ancients Trilogy=== Following the success of the mission, she and Rhonin were tasked with touring the Alliance and reminding everyone that there were other threats in the world besides orcs that would have to be faced sooner or later.''[[The Well of Eternity]]'', pg. 14 Along with Rhonin and Krasus, Vereesa was among the few well-known survivors of the Scourge that destroyed Lordaeron, Dalaran, and Quel'Thalas after the corruption of Prince Arthas. The rest of her family was not so lucky. They were one of the hardest hit by the Scourge invasion into Quel'Thalas. Sylvanas was killed by Arthas Menethil and raised as a banshee in his service, later becoming Banshee Queen of the Forsaken, and Vereesa learned from her grandfather that he had to slay the ghoulish corpse of his own son, her uncle. From him she had also heard how her younger brother had been ripped apart by a hungering mob of undead led by their own elder brother who was then himself burned with the rest of the Scourge by elven resistance fighters. Her parents' fate was unknown, but they, too, were presumed dead.''[[The Well of Eternity]]'', pg. 16 - 17 While she and her husband, Rhonin, were preparing for the birth of their twin offspring, Rhonin was once again summoned by Krasus for help. As a reward for Rhonin's courage, Nozdormu allowed Rhonin to return to Vereesa at the moment she went into labor to ensure he would not miss a moment of the twins' lives. Nozdormu also offered the children the friendship of the bronze dragonflight. A human named Jalia assisted in the birth. ===Mysteries of Azeroth=== Following the fall of Silvermoon, Vereesa took it upon herself to gather those she could find, and set out to reclaim the outpost of [[Alah'Thalas]] in the [[Thalassian Highlands]]. Though it was not an easy task, it gave the displaced high elves a place to call home.{{questlong|Alliance|26|The Kaldorei Problem}} ''([https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?quest=40376 Deprecated])'' From there, as the Speaker of the Silvermoon Remnant, she sought to bring her people closer to the Alliance. However, as the resettlement of the Highlands progressed, surviving members of the nobility deposed her as leader of the Remnant, forming the [[Regency Council]] in place of the Speaker. Vereesa, as a member of the prestigious Windrunner family, was granted a place amongst the Council. In the aftermath of the formation of the Council, Vereesa formed the [[Silver Covenant]], a political faction loyal to her vision for the future of the high elves.{{Alliance}} [5] [[The Silver Covenant]] Under her leadership, the Silver Covenant was successful in its second attempt to reclaim [[Shalandis Isle]], and Vereesa stepped foot in Eversong for the first time in eight years. Vereesa sought to use the prestige of her victory to reclaim her title as Speaker. However, this victory was bought through the diverting of funds intended for the Regency Council and the people of the Silvermoon Remnant. As such, it undercut the Covenant's victory and sabotaged Vereesa's attempt to reclaim her position when the matter was brought to light by Lord [[Astalor Sunsworn]]. To her horror, her victory was shattered before her as Lord Sunsworn then took the opportunity to motion the Council to be elevated to Lord-Regent of Quel'Thalas, having acquired the five votes necessary from his fellow council members - with even Lor'themar casting his vote for Lord Sunsworn.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u90BCZfygz0 A GOOD DAY — Everlook Broadcasting Co. Radio Play Series] ==Quests== * {{questlong|Alliance|5|Message for the Windrunner}} {{questfinish}} * {{questlong|Alliance|5|The Silver Covenant}} {{queststart}} * {{questlong|Alliance|9|Back to Lady Windrunner}} {{questfinish}} * {{questlong|Alliance|9|Rommath, the Traitor}} {{queststart}} * {{questlong|Alliance|9|Rommath, the Saviour}} {{questfinish}} ==Quotes== ===Gossip=== In our people's most trying times, it was my unwavering commitment that brought us together to forge this sanctuary of hope. Through earnest efforts, I mended the bonds between our kin and the Alliance, restoring the trust that had faltered. I never sought regal titles or aspirations of grandeur, merely recognizing the pressing need for steadfast leadership. Yet, in the halls of our own kin, where nobility should be defined by honor and foresight, a blindness persists. The noble families, entangled in the webs of influence and wealth, fail to perceive the true nature of our collective journey. Unjustly stripped of the title of Speaker, a position embraced not for personal gain but for the welfare of our people, I stand witness to a disheartening diversion of focus. Instead of marshalling our resources and collective wisdom to face the pressing challenges that loom before us, we find ourselves mired in needless debates that obscure the clarity of our path forward. ===On-click=== ;Greeting * Welcome to Alah'Thalas. * Greetings, friend. * Quel'Thalas will not be forgotten. * Have you come to help us? ;Pissed * Is there something wrong? * I have left my husband behind for my people. * My people needed me. '''Voren'thal the Scryer''' is a magister<ref name="A Good Day"/> and former advisor to Prince [[Kael'thas Sunstrider]], and a current member of the [[Regency Council]] of [[Alah'Thalas]]. He has long lived under the roof of Lord [[Astalor Sunsworn]] in Alah'Thalas, enjoying his patronage and basking in borrowed wealth and influence, and is believed to be nothing more than a puppet to Lord Sunsworn.<ref name="A Good Day"/>

When Lord Sunsworn made a motion before the Council to be named Lord-Regent of Quel'Thalas following the retaking of [[Shalandis Isle]] by the [[Silver Covenant]], Voren'thal voted in his favor.<ref name="A Good Day"/>

==Quotes==
In a bygone era, I stood as the closest confidant and advisor to Prince Kael'thas, watching with sorrow as he forsook us, seduced by the malevolent powers of the Legion.

Though I yearn for his return, the wisps of foresight that caress my ancient senses reveal a path fraught with uncertainty.

Hope lingers, but I am no fool. In the absence of our prince, we must face the harsh reality and select a temporary leader to guide our people through these tumultuous times.

'''Vorgendor''' (also called the '''Blood Dimension''') is the mysterious [[worgen]] home-world.<ref name=":0">[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?object=2020126 Vorgendor: The Blood Dimension]</ref> Once a realm where [[Elune]]'s favored servants lived freely, an invasion from the [[Burning Legion]] resulted in the corruption of the world; in a desperate bid to fend off the demonic invaders, the worgen forsook Elune in favour of blood magic, tainting the once-blessed race.

== History ==
Originally a world where the worgen walked in harmony under the light of Elune, the encroachment of the Burning Legion (referred to as the Lords of the Emerald Flame by [[Velinde Starsong]]<ref>[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=5520 Velinde's Journal]</ref>) drove the worgen to using blood magic. Despite the dark powers at their command, the worgen are fighting a losing battle against the Legion.<ref name=":0" /> Vorgendor is described in Ur's texts as a dark place of nightmares,<ref>[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=6283 The Book of Ur]</ref> likely reflecting the Legion's invasion and the worgen's subsequent corruption.

At some point during the height of the Kaldorei Empire, Queen Azshara and her Highborne mages delved into forbidden arts, including opening passageways to Vorgendor.<ref>{{Neutral}} [https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=41067 Scythe of the Goddess]</ref>

WIM (WoW Instant Messenger) is an instant messenger interface designed specifically for in-game whispers. It allows you to communicate without interfering with your busy interface during raids, providing the convenience of a dedicated chat window for each user you communicate with. == Installation == '''GitAddonsManager (Recommended)''' The easiest way to keep WIM up to date is by using [[GitAddonsManager]]. # '''Add the Repository:''' Add the following URL to GitAddonsManager: https://github.com/refaim/WIM.git # '''Select the Branch:''' Ensure that the master branch is selected. # '''Update:''' Using GitAddonsManager, you can check for and install updates for all your AddOns with a single click. '''Manual Installation''' If you prefer manual installation, follow these steps: # Go to the main page of the repository. # Click the '''<> Code''' dropdown and download the repository as a .zip. # Unpack the .zip and rename the folder to WIM, removing the -master suffix. # Move the folder into your Interface/AddOns directory and restart the game. == Git Links == [https://github.com/refaim/WIM '''(refaim)'''] == Commands == * '''/wim''': Option Window * '''/wim history''': History Viewer * '''/wim help''': Info window * '''/wim reset''': Reset all options to default * '''/wim reset filters''': Reload all built in filter definitions * '''/wim clear history''': Clear history '''Shift + Left Click:''' * '''On Minimap Icon''': Drag the minimap icon when in free-moving mode. * '''On Inventory Items''': Insert the item link into the message box (for items in the inventory, trading, looting, etc.). * '''On Trade Skills and Crafts''': Insert links for selected trade skills and craft reagents into the message box. * '''On Loot Items''': Insert the loot item link into the message box. '''Tab:''' Toggle between messages while in a conversation window. '''Whisper:''' * Click on the name of the person you want to whisper to in the chat * (/w): Send a whisper message to a player. '''Reply:''' * (/r): Reply to the last whispered message. == Velvy Wintergarde ==
{{Character|name=Velvy Wintergarde|image=Velvy_portrait_1.png|aliases=The Pearl|titles=Baroness Wintergarde|faction=Chaotic Neutral|affiliation=Warlock Circle|faffiliation=The Kingdom of Alterac,

To the world, the young Velvy is a traveling enchanter, arcaneweaver, and magical artifacts dealer. Beneath this guise, she is a trained warlock and holds a Baroness title of a fallen Alterac house. One might find Velvy anywhere in Azeroth, gathering rare relics and lost knowledge, or perhaps spending lavishly on the finest suite of a tavern.

=== Appearance ===
Velvy resembles the pale elegance of an alabaster statue, with her ivory skin, silver-white mane and eyes of the same sterling hue. These unique features are a permanent mark of the dark ritual she endured at the age of ten, during which the communion with a demon stripped most of the color from her. Her original appearance is long lost to memory.

Her features are delicate, with long eyelashes, a slightly upturned nose, and lips the color of cherries. She wears a bloodstone as a pendant resting on her neckline and paints her fingernails a matching shade of red. The crimson of her lips, the bloodstone, and her nails creates a striking embellishment against the canvas of her pale form.

Velvy’s lithe, slender figure that hints at a youth spent in hardship. Her height and weight are below average for her age, and her poor physical stamina leaves her prone to exhaustion and illness. People often mistake her for a child because of her petite frame, a misconception she often takes advantage of rather than address. She frequently uses magic to compensate for physical frailties, which has given her a unique and profound insight into the arts of life drain.

Velvy possesses an exquisite slender kiseru pipe, crafted from fine silver and bamboo, which she uses for smoking during her moments of leisure. The aromatic smoke helps to mask the sulfuric scent of fel magic, putting her at ease while concealing her warlock identity from others. Fermented Dreamfoil petal is her signature tobacco, which is expensive, but leaves a faint, lingering sweet fragrance on her person.

=== '''Personality''' ===
Velvy projects a practiced aloofness and a detached air, but she is not a cold person. Those who have earned her friendship discover a softer side, along with a resilient optimism and a wicked sense of humor. She is often cynical and highly perceptive of shifting dynamics and burgeoning conspiracies, allowing her to anticipate trouble. In her daily life, she prefers an existence of freedom, leisure, and ease.

She dislikes chatter. In most situations, she is a listener and an actor, rarely one for persuasion. By the same token, she is seldom moved by the silver tongues of others. Unless she takes a personal interest in someone, suitors find her exceptionally difficult to please. Those who do capture her favor, however, are rewarded with unexpected generosity.

Velvy loves money and material comforts. While her skills in enchanting and appraising artifacts provide a handsome income, she is not above using illicit means to make a profit. Yet she is no miser. She spends her gold lavishly and often donates what she cannot spend to those in need.

She is meticulous about her body, bathing frequently whenever possible and deliberately avoiding manual labor. Her posture and mannerisms are rooted in her aristocratic upbringing in Alterac. Such ingrained grace allows her to move effortlessly through high society, creating many opportunities for her pursuits.

=== Abilities and Skills ===
From her mentor Menara, Velvy inherited the craft of Arcaneweave, a specialized technique of weaving raw magic into threads. The garments created through this art are prized by Azeroth's spellcasters as superior power conduits and can also be used to create enchanted, coded correspondence. Complementing this, Velvy’s profound knowledge of enchanting and her expertise in appraising magical artifacts allow her to identify high-value items on her travels and trade them for a significant profit. Together, these skills form the bedrock of her legitimate public identity.

Beneath this facade, however, Velvy is a naturally gifted and well-trained warlock, with a remarkable specialization in the arts of life drain and transference. Aided by her bloodstone, she also maintains a firm command over demons, allowing her to solve many troubles that arise from her lifestyle.

During the dark ritual conducted when she was ten, her father failed in his attempt to directly summon a Sayaad. He resorted instead to using Velvy's body as a physical vessel for the demon. Though the ritual was interrupted and the Sayaad later banished by Menara, the demonic communion left an indelible mark on Velvy. It imbued her with a subtly seductive aura, capable of enthralling those with weaker wills. This dark legacy has also, to some degree, shaped her personality.

== Background story ==
Velvy Wintergarde was born seven years after the opening of the Dark Portal, the sole heir to the noble House Wintergarde of Alterac. By then, the Second War had concluded. Due to Lord Perenolde's betrayal of the Alliance, the entire kingdom of Alterac was occupied and dismantled. A year after Velvy's birth, House Wintergarde, like all Alterac nobility, was stripped of its lands. In the years that followed, they were absorbed into the criminal organization known as the Syndicate.

Though the old nobles of the Syndicate had lost their fortunes, they remained dedicated to restoring their rule. They invested heavily in raising their successors, which plunged Velvy into a childhood of jarring contradictions. She was often shuffled between bandit hideouts in the cold mountain valleys, living a life less stable than that of a Lordaeron peasant. Simultaneously, she received a formal aristocratic education, meant to instill in her a sense of nobility, superiority, and her inherent right to rule the frigid mountains and the wretches who remained there. Many of her peers internalized such logic after a single raid on a farming village. To Velvy, it was always absurd. She could never reconcile her miserable reality and the vile acts of her kin with the high-minded ideals she was taught. Nor could she see the value in the ogre-infested lands her father haggled over with her betrothed's family. Velvy quickly learned to ignore such delusions, focusing instead on the heavy tomes plundered from Dalaran caravans. The texts were far too advanced for a child, but they gave her mind a place to retreat from the absurdity of her world.

When Velvy was ten, Lordaeron was thrown into turmoil by the re-emerging Horde, an event the Syndicate viewed as an opportunity. A cult of warlocks called the Argus Wake grew in influence within the Syndicate, offering powerful Bloodstones as conduits for dark power. Many, including Velvy’s father, Baron Wintergarde, were seduced by their promises of ultimate strength. The Baron’s forces had suffered greatly in skirmishes with Lordaeron's military, and his calculus was grimly simple: the Bloodstone required a blood sacrifice, and what blood was more potent than his own line? Velvy was to be the offering.

However, Velvy was no lamb for the slaughter. Her studious nature had allowed her to discern her father's intentions as he prepared the ritual. She did not foresee the full extent of his depravity. He sought not just her blood, but her very flesh and soul as a vessel for a summoned demon. Instead of fleeing, Velvy spotted a flaw in the ritual's design. As a Sayaad was drawn forth to claim her, she seized the moment and offered the demon a far more tempting bargain. The ritual was twisted on its head. Baron Wintergarde and his acolytes became the sacrifice, their lives feeding the Bloodstone.

Clutching the empowered artifact and shielded by her new demonic pact, Velvy escaped the Alterac Mountains. But the pact was unstable. When the demon sensed her weakness and moved to claim everything, it was Menara Voidrender who intervened. A warlock who had long been stealing secrets from the Argus Wake, Menara saved Velvy from the greedy demon's grasp and became Velvy’s mentor, teaching her the ways of a warlock in exchange for the Bloodstone. For the next several years, the pair traveled widely, posing as Arcaneweavers from Dalaran or dealers of magic artifacts.

In the 20th year after the Dark Portal's opening, facing the relentless Scourge, Menara and Velvy joined Jaina Proudmoore's expedition to Kalimdor. Under Jaina’s leadership in the fledgling city of Theramore, experienced spellcasters and enchanters like Menara and Tabetha quickly proved their worth. As a gifted apprentice, Velvy naturally found her place among them. Her unique appearance and alluring presence earned her the nickname "The Pearl" among the Theramore sailors, none of whom suspected her connection to fel magic.

A year later, the Battle of Mount Hyjal erupted. At fourteen, Velvy was deemed too inexperienced for the front lines. But the spoils of war, artifacts of the Burning Legion, proved invaluable to her and Menara’s secret studies. This period ignited Velvy’s profound understanding of life transference and demonology. By sixteen, she was a capable warlock in her own right. But with her rise came danger. Rumors of dark magic practitioners in Theramore began to circulate, and the city was no longer safe.

In the 22nd year, Daelin Proudmoore's arrival sparked a ruinous war. Menara and Velvy had already foreseen the coming trouble and fled Theramore, escaping the conflict entirely. They made their way to Ratchet. The free-wheeling goblin town offered a haven where they could continue their work in peace. In Ratchet, however, Velvy honed her skills in enchanting and appraising magical artifacts more than the forbidden arts. Among goblins, such talents were far more profitable than dabbling in fel. Before she turned eighteen, she had amassed a considerable fortune, enough to travel with the affluence of a true noblewoman.

In the 25th year, Velvy bid farewell to her mentor to forge her own path. She planned to sail for Booty Bay and try her luck in the Eastern Kingdoms, where no one knew her name. As a final blessing and a mark of her graduation, Menara returned the Bloodstone to her.

The [[Voidwalker]] is the second [[Pet|pet]] available to the [[Warlock]]. It becomes availiable at level 10 after completing a series of [[Quest|quests]].

The first pet available to the Warlock is an [[Imp]], while the third pet is the [[Succubus]].

Voidwalkers are good [[Tank|tankers]] against non-[[Elite|elite]] [[mob]]s at or near the Warlock's level; therefore, they are excellent for solo play, or when a party tank is unavailable.

Among the four regular Warlock pets, the Voidwalker has the most [[health]], but the least [[mana]].

The Voidwalker requires a [[Soul Shard]] to [[Summon|summon]].  It is the first Warlock pet to require one; the acquisition of the Voidwalker coincides with the acquisition of the ability to collect Soul Shards (with [[Drain Soul]]).

== Acquiring ==

As usual, the quest line begins with an [[NPC]] Warlock near the [[trainer]]s in one of each faction's major cities.  When you reach level 10 as a Warlock, go to any Warlock training area for your faction (other than the level 1-6 starting areas) and there will be a quest for you, either starting you on the quest or directing you to the right person to talk to.  For the [[Horde]], Ophek in [[Razor Hill]] will send you to Gan'rul Bloodeye in [[Orgrimmar]], and Ageron Kargal in [[Brill]] will send you to Carendin Halgar in [[The Undercity]].  [[Alliance]] Warlocks will be directed to Gakin the Darkbinder in [[Stormwind]], either by Remen Marcot of [[Goldshire]] or Lago Blackwrench of [[Ironforge]] (to whom you may be directed by the [[Gnome]] Warlock trainers of [[Kharanos]]).  In any case, the questgiver will send you to retrieve a quest item from someone nearby, who will not part with it willingly, and when you return with it, the ritual begins.  A trainer will summon a Voidwalker, and you must defeat it to earn the power to summon one yourself.  Others can assist, of course.

== Voidwalker Tips ==

The Voidwalker is a great tank pet; he takes massive amounts of damage, has great armor, holds massive amounts of enemy aggression (which is nice because it's not on you!) and heals himself quickly after every fight.  If you intend to fight multiple enemies simultaneously, the Voidwalker is your best choice.  If you spend a few talent points in [[Warlock Talents#Improved Voidwalker|Improved Voidwalker]], he can keep the attention of even the highest level enemies.  His Sacrifice is great when being ambushed by another player or mob, giving you a shield that can absorb thousands of points of damage at a moment's notice.

Sadly, the Voidwalker does the least melee damage of any of the regular 4 Warlock pets.  Don't rely on it to kill the target with melee damage.  Instead, put your [[DoT]]s on the [[mob]], and maybe use some direct-damage spells as well, such as [[Immolate]] or [[Shadow Bolt]], but be sparing so you don't draw the aggro to yourself.  The whole point of a Voidwalker is to absorb the mob's attention and damage so you're free to let your spells work, watch for adds, use [[Life Tap]], bandage yourself, etc.

Besides increasing its threat generation powers, the Improved Voidwalker talent also amplifies the self-healing effect of Consume Shadows and the damage absorption of Sacrifice.

If you're going to be facing just one mob at a time, turn off the auto-cast on Suffering.  There's no sense wasting mana doing an [[Area of Effect|area-of-effect]] taunt when you're using a single-target one too.  An exception to this would be at high levels when Torment just isn't keeping the aggro off you, but even then, Suffering doesn't help much if that's the case.

Torment and Suffering have absolutely no use in PvP combat.  If you know in advance that you're going to be engaging in PvP and are still determined to have the Voidwalker around for some reason, turn off auto-cast on these abilities so you'll at least have plenty of mana for Consume Shadows.

Because of its high health and Consume Shadows ability, the Voidwalker is likely to have a lot of health at any given time, making it the best pet to have around if you're going to use [[Warlock Talents#Soul Link|Soul Link]], especially if you also have [[Warlock Talents#Fel Stamina|Fel Stamina]].  However, because of its low mana and high mana usage, this is a terrible pet to have around if you're going to use [[Warlock Talents#Dark Pact|Dark Pact]].

The Voidwalker's benefits under the [[Warlock Talents#Demonic Sacrifice|Demonic Sacrifice]] and [[Warlock Talents#Master Demonologist|Master Demonologist]] talents (rapid health regeneration and damage reduction, respectively) can add to a Warlock's survival chances in many situations.

== Description ==
{{Character|name=Ventya|image=Ventya_Phantom.png|titles=The Dark Rider|faction=Chaotic Neutral|affiliation=|faffiliation=Darkmoon Faire, Karazhan|occupation=Treasure Hunter|status=Alive|birthPlace=|race=Half Elf (Humanoid)|gender=Female|height=5'4''|eyes=Blue|hair=Chestnut|imagecaption=Ventya launching an ambush from the Void.}}

Ventya is an unshackled Dark Rider and an enigma that defies definition. Her public persona is that of a neutral treasure hunter, but she is simultaneously a dancer, epicure, thief, spy, ghost, assassin, and an informant for SI:7. Evidence suggests she still acquires various magical artifacts and brings them to the Tower of Karazhan, but as long as one does not stand in her way, she is generally harmless to most.

=== Appearance ===
In her natural state, Ventya appears as a young female half-elf, meaning she has shorter pointed ears and eyebrows, faintly glowing blue eyes, soft facial contours, and a pert nose. Her skin is pale as alabaster, and she has voluminous chestnut hair reaching her back, though it is usually tied into a high ponytail. Standing at 5'4", her physique is lithe and flexible, with long limbs and low body fat, allowing her to perform many contortions and movements impossible for ordinary people.

In her daily life, Ventya dresses in a low-profile and modest manner. While traveling, her signature attire is an oversized woolen shawl that drapes from her neck down to mid-thigh, concealing her entire torso and whatever objects she wishes to hide. Beneath this, her inner wear varies, but typically consists of a loose shirt, cropped trousers, and short leather boots.

For more professional occasions, however, she retains the Dark Riders' black form-fitting light armor. Yet she has replaced their signature black hooded cloak with a scarlet one, resembling a streak of flame crawling up the night.

Like all Dark Riders, Ventya is not undead in the strictest sense. People can see her enjoying mortal food, and some describe her body as being as cool as a sleeper.

Ventya possesses an enchanted pocket watch warped by Medivh into a "Phasic Anchor," which allows her to temporarily banish herself—partially or entirely—from the material plane. This enables her to appear as a translucent phantom or vanish completely when needed. However, this ability occasionally causes anomalies in her appearance and her connection to time.

=== Personality ===
Ventya's personality is free-spirited, laid-back, and relaxed, making her seem approachable. She frequently shows appreciation for all the beautiful and pleasant things in daily life, retaining a childlike sense of fun.

Internally, her philosophical core is a natural existentialist stance and a Nietzschean master morality; her unwavering subjectivity is almost impossible to be shaken by the outside world.

Ventya can maintain a relaxed and calm mindset even in extreme situations. She appreciates professionalism and inherits the strict self-discipline from her time as a dancer, demonstrating extreme professional competence in body management, equipment maintenance, and operational details. But what truly makes her stand out is her unshackled wit and astonishing audacity.
[[File:Ventya Relax.png|left|thumb|Ventya delivering an artifact weapon.]]
Ventya has a poor memory; remembering names and dates long-term has always been a challenge for her. Her concepts of royalty, nationhood, and law are faint, yet she possesses a precise judgment and understanding of the underlying logic of interests and power behind them.

Though she has already secured her freedom from Karazhan's shackles, in pursuit of more, Ventya continuously seeks liberation from Sargeras's curse—a curse that compels her to constantly seek out precious magical artifacts, only to ultimately cast them into the void of Karazhan. This means that even as an excellent treasure hunter, she never gets the lion's share. Because of this, Ventya will not hesitate to strike deals with any faction holding forbidden knowledge, from trolls and dragons to the undead Scourge.

To avoid trouble, Ventya usually dodges topics related to her true identity and history, only vaguely stating that she works for a wealthy collector. Nevertheless, she once confessed to being a Dark Rider while deep in her cups. People laughed it off as a tall tale, but the moniker stuck as a nickname among adventurers.

=== Capabilities & Skills ===
'''Foundations''': Ventya is a fast learner, allowing her to benefit greatly from every stage of her life. She began training with the Darkmoon Faire at age 10 and became an excellent dancer. During her travels, she mastered survival skills passed down by travelers and local inhabitants, as well as several languages.

'''Dark Blessing''': The Dark Titan's curse transformed Ventya into a Dark Rider, specifically specialized in infiltration and assassination to serve as a spy within their ranks. Additionally, as the calling of a Dark Rider, Ventya is skilled in tracking and appraising magical artifacts.

'''Phasic Anchor''': An enchanted pocket watch that was once used to ensure she could never escape Karazhan's binding, no matter how far she roamed; otherwise, she would be banished from the material world entirely. However, once Ventya became the master of this item, it lost its purpose as a shackle. Through study, she can manipulate the watch to achieve controlled self-banishment. This allows her to appear and disappear like a ghost, pass through obstacles, and makes her nearly impossible to trap. But this ability is unstable and often comes with a price. Clearly, she has not yet fully fathomed its secrets, nor does she know the consequences of abusing it. On the other hand, whoever possesses this pocket watch holds Ventya's fate in their hands—if they can survive her pursuit.

'''Secrets of the Realm''': During her 20 years bound to the Tower of Karazhan, Ventya befriended every ghostly guest. She learned almost all the secrets these former nobles and royals were supposed to take to their graves, some of which could make a political earthquake. After regaining her freedom, she traded some of these secrets for the protection and assistance of SI:7. Furthermore, she learned high-society etiquette from those ghosts, allowing her to flawlessly disguise herself as a noblewoman.


== Background Story ==

=== Life as Dandelion ===
Ventya was raised in a place of legends: the Dalaran Orphanage, the cradle of the first Guardian of Tirisfal. Yet, this pedigree did not make her special. Before her tenth birthday, she lacked even a name. People casually referred to her as "Violet," a generic moniker tossed at any nameless stray wandering the streets of the magocratic city.

As a quintessential "Dalaran specialty"—a half-human, half-elf child with at least one magically gifted parent, possessing nothing but an inherited pocket watch—she was expected to have a promising career as a mage. However, when she was ten, the Darkmoon Faire visited the city. Silas Darkmoon took a keen interest in the young half-elf. Ventya remains convinced that the orphanage matron made a hefty profit from the transaction. Silas, on the other hand, saw her rarity and potential; he knew that with rigorous training, she could be molded into a future superstar.[[File:Ventya Faire F.png|thumb|250x250px|Ventya backstage at the Darkmoon Faire.]]

Given the stage name "Ventya," the girl grew up aboard caravans, blooming alongside the flora of the myriad lands they traversed. Though she initially felt deeply ashamed, and the grueling training brought her immense suffering, time proved Silas right. Ventya was gradually forged into an utterly captivating dancer. Her youth was adorned with endless applause and showers of flowers. She ceased to care whether she was viewed as a half-breed freak, instead basking in the adoration and spotlight. The nomadic life cultivated her carefree, easygoing nature. In a poet's terms, she had been wedded to the wind long before she ever shed her first blood.
=== Dancing with Shadows ===
Nine years of freedom and blossoming passed. One day, a merchant caravan shared a camp with the Faire. There, the merchants presented Ventya with an opportunity: they were bound for the Kingdom of Stormwind to conduct business with Medivh. Knowing the Guardian's recent reputation for throwing extravagantly opulent parties, they were certain he would generously reward a dancer of her caliber.

The titles of Royal Mage of Stormwind and Guardian of Azeroth carried an intoxicating weight, and Ventya decided to seize the chance. Despite Silas's cautious reservations, she was determined to chase that glory. She reasoned that if she returned with a purse bursting with gold, Silas couldn't stay mad for long. Thus, on the day the Faire and the caravan parted ways, Ventya slipped away in secret.

The caravan's leader, Ariden, was exceedingly hospitable to Ventya on the road to Karazhan. The reality, however, was far more sinister—they were nothing but a band of charlatans. Ariden intended to peddle counterfeit magical artifacts to the Guardian, using Ventya merely as a gift and a stepping stone to gain an audience.

No one knew at the time that the Guardian was already possessed by Sargeras. Ariden's pathetic ruse was instantly seen through. The Dark Titan's wrath manifested as a devastating curse that descended upon them all, Ventya included. From that moment on, there were no more charlatans or dancers—only the Dark Riders, spectral terrors haunting rainy nights, cursed to hunt for genuine magical artifacts for their master forever. As for Ventya, Medivh seized her inherited pocket watch and warped it into a phasic anchor. Her very soul was "tethered" to the timepiece. No matter how far she roamed, she must eventually return to wherever the watch was kept. Should its hands ever stop, she would be banished from this world entirely.
[[File:Ventya Darkrider F.png|thumb|250x250px|'''Ventya among the Dark Riders.'''|left]]
For many years that followed, Ventya and her cursed brethren stole and plundered magical artifacts across the world, leaving terrifying legends in their wake. Ironically, Ventya might have been the only Dark Rider to find enjoyment in this fate. For someone who started with nothing, every step was a step up. Once merely a plaything meant to entertain, she now wielded formidable power, wore a wicked black cloak, and rode a nightmarish steed that answered only to her. Where people once looked at her with disdain, curiosity, or lust, their gazes were now filled with profound terror. This made her feel strangely fulfilled and respected... even if she couldn't tell whether this satisfaction stemmed from mind control or her own genuine feelings.

Three years after the opening of the Dark Portal, Medivh was slain by Khadgar and Lothar, leaving Karazhan abandoned. However, the resurrected castellan Moroes took possession of Ventya’s pocket watch, ensuring her predicament remained entirely unchanged. Yet, true to her nature, Ventya always found value in living. Between fulfilling her duties as a Dark Rider, she turned the haunting tower into her personal playground.[[File:Ventya Ball F.png|thumb|250x250px|'''Ventya is to blame for much of the mess adventurers would behold years later.''']]

Over the next nearly twenty years, the absence of a master allowed her to brazenly indulge in the tower's luxurious amenities and wine cellars, causing endless trouble for Moroes. Though the atmosphere was macabre, for a freak caught between the living and the dead, this was hardly a flaw. She mingled with all the ghosts, attended spectral balls, and hosted performances, fulfilling her dream of dancing for the dignitaries of the southern kingdoms. But two decades is enough to grind down any enthusiasm. The longer this madness lasted, the more she missed the mundane days on the wind. She plotted countless heists to steal back her watch—her freedom—but as the kingdom's finest castellan, Moroes never gave her a opening.
=== Phantom Liberty ===
An age seemed to pass until one day, strike teams from the Alliance and the Horde breached the tower, conquering the chaos within and striking down Moroes. One of the adventurers claimed the pocket watch as a trophy. Ventya, who was on an expedition far away, sensed this immediately and recognized it as her golden opportunity. She defected from the Dark Riders on the spot, struck down those who tried to intercept her, and set off to hunt down the one who held her tether.

With the tracking instincts of a Dark Rider, she swiftly pinpointed the watch's location. Unfortunately, the adventurer died shortly after in a skirmish with the Scarlet Crusade, and the watch was taken to Tyr's Hand. Left with no other choice, Ventya attempted to infiltrate the zealots' stronghold to steal it back.

It was a trap, however. The Crusaders ambushed and captured Ventya in a decoy vault, imprisoning her within. The Crusade's arcanists had long sensed the bizarre power radiating from the watch, but they never expected to reel in such a unique prize—a creature entirely unlike any plaguebearer or undead they had ever faced. This piqued the inquisitors' morbid curiosity. Ventya endured weeks of torture and experimentation, subjected to such massive doses of searing Holy Light that it even revitalized the senses and emotions that the curse had numbed. Ironically, this agony restored her mortal instincts, allowing her to smell an approaching thunderstorm. On that stormy night, she managed to seduce and kill her guard, finally reclaiming her watch and escaping Tyr's Hand into the pouring rain, where her loyal and scary steed, Nightmare, waited amidst the thunder.

With the watch back in her possession, Ventya is no longer tethered to Karazhan; she finally has her freedom. Yet, the Dark Titan's curse remains absolute. To this day, she continues to sporadically hunt magical artifacts and deliver them to the tower. Despite sharing the same objective, she has seemingly broken with Ariden and the other Dark Riders. They frequently ambush her in places like Duskwood and Deadwind Pass, seeking to punish her defection and snatch her artifacts. But to this day, they have yet to successfully catch their sister who is best at vanishing.

==As a quest objective==
* {{questlong|Neutral|60|Scythe of the Goddess (7)|Scythe of the Goddess}}

==Contains==
{{Book|content=
I dedicated the entirety of my scholarly endeavours to the unraveling of the enigmas shrouded within the so-called Vorgendor, a Blood World nestled far in the Dark Beyond. This quest of mine led me through shadowed corridors of knowledge, where oft I found myself ensnared by the seductive whispers of Blood Magic. Yet, with steadfast resolve, I stand before thee, a humble chronicler, ready to unveil the saga of Vorgendor and its ancient myths.
----
Vorgendor, a realm fraught with peril, is home to the bloodthirsty worgen, lupine beings consumed by an insatiable bloodlust. In their society, blood magic reigns supreme, wielded as a weapon to obliterate foes and subjugate the feeble. This dark art is a blight upon their culture, embraced in desperation to fend off the Emerald Flame, a sinister force that voraciously seeks to consume their world.
----
Astute readers may find the term 'Emerald Flame' vaguely familiar, for indeed, this malevolent force is none other than the Burning Legion, a mysterious power that once brought the orcs to our own realm. The worgen of Vorgendor have waged an unending war against the Legion for years, a struggle they are gradually losing, despite resorting to magics as dark as those wielded by their adversaries.
----
In my scholarly pursuit, I sought to unearth more than merely the blood magics that now dominate worgen society. I yearned to discover their origins, who they were before the blight of the Emerald Flame. Through the scant information salvaged from ancient scrolls and the visions that haunted my slumbers, I learned that in a time long forgotten, the Worgen held the Moon in reverence, akin to the elves of yore.
----
They spoke of a blue moon that once danced across their skies, an entity they worshipped and adored as a divine goddess. This celestial bond intrigued me, for it bore an uncanny resemblance to our own Azeroth's blue moon, which emerges in the heavens during our most dire epochs. Could it be that the blue moon of Vorgendor and ours are one and the same?

Venturing into the depths of Vorgendor, risking both life and sanity, I beheld their heavens, yet the sight that greeted me was not of a tranquil blue, but a blood-red moon, casting a crimson pall over their world.
----
Yet, all hope was not lost. Fortune allowed me to commune with one of their blood mages. The particulars of this rendezvous must remain shrouded in secrecy, for such knowledge must never be allowed to taint the hands of malevolence. Nevertheless, be assured, I was privy to a prophecy: the return of their Moon Goddess, heralding salvation. This prophecy foretold of a day when the Blue Moon would reappear, opening a gateway to a new realm, untouched by the Emerald Flame, where the worgen might thrive a new.
----
They believed the Blue Moon would guide them to this sanctum, leaving me to ponder—a portentous thought—whether it might lead them to our world. Thus, I caution thee, beware the Blue Child, for it signals the advent of the worgen into our realm. This celestial harbinger, once a beacon of hope for a beleaguered race, now casts a shadow over our own fate. Should the prophecy come to pass, and the gateway between our worlds be rent asunder, we must prepare for the eventuality of their arrival.
----
As I pen these words, my quill trembles, not our of fear, but with the weight of responsibility. The knowledge I have gleamed through my arduous journey—through forbidden tomes, whispered secrets of the arcane, and visions granted by the very fabric of magic itself—must serve as a beacon to those who would stand against the darkness.
----
Let it be known that the worgen, though driven to desperation by their battle against the Emerald Flame, harbor within them the potential for both destruction and redemption. Their society, once illuminated by the gentle glow of the moon they venerated, now lies in the shadow of blood magic. Yet, the prophecy speaks of a rebirth, a chance for salvation not just for the worgen, but perhaps for our world as well.
----
In closing this tome, I implore thee, dear reader, to heed the lessons contained within these aged pages. The tale of Vorgendor is more than a mere chronicle of otherworldly beings and arcane mysteries; it is a warning. As we gaze upon the night sky, let us not forget the potential for worlds beyond our own to touch upon our fates. We must remain vigilant, for the cosmos is vast, and its secrets are myriad.
----
And so, I lay down my quill, my life's work etched into the parchment of this tome. May these words endure as a testament to my journey into the dark beyond, a journey that has shown me the thin veil that separates our world from others, teeming with beings both majestic and terrifying. Beware the Blue Child, for its light may herald the dawn of a new age, or the twilight of our own.

In eternal pursuit of knowledge and in solemn warning,

[[Ur]], Chronicler of the Dark Beyond, Guardian of Forgotten Lore
}}
